Home.tilesHeading: What do you need help with?

family.title: Family visas
family.summary: Some U.S. citizens and permanent residents can ask the government to let close family members come to or stay in the United States.

greenCard.title: Green card
greenCard.summary: A green card lets a person live and work in the United States permanently. There are different ways to qualify.

citizenship.title: Citizenship
citizenship.summary: Many green card holders can apply to become U.S. citizens after meeting certain rules.

protection.title: Asylum and protection
protection.summary: People who fear harm in their home country may be able to ask for protection in the United States. Deadlines can be strict.

court.title: Immigration court
court.summary: If you received papers telling you to go to immigration court, do not ignore them. Missing a court date can cause serious problems.

Emergency.title: Detained or arrested? Get help now
Emergency.lead: Stay calm. Call us first. Then read the steps below.
Emergency.rights1: You have the right to stay silent. You can say: “I want to remain silent. I want to speak to a lawyer.”
Emergency.rights2: Do not sign any paper you do not understand. Ask to speak to a lawyer first.
Emergency.rights3: Do not lie and do not show false papers.
Emergency.rights4: Do not run and do not fight. Keep your hands where officers can see them.
Emergency.rights5: If officers come to your home, you do not have to open the door unless they show a warrant signed by a judge. Ask them to pass it under the door or hold it to a window.
Emergency.familyTitle: If someone you love was detained
Emergency.family1: Call us. Tell us the person’s full name, date of birth, and country of birth.
Emergency.family2: If you know it, write down where and when the person was taken.
Emergency.family3: If the person has immigration papers, find them and keep them safe. Do not send them to anyone until a lawyer asks.
Emergency.family4: You can search for a person held by ICE on the government’s online detainee locator.
Emergency.prepare1: Memorize one phone number you can call.
Emergency.prepare2: Keep our phone number with you.
Emergency.prepare3: Make a plan for who will care for your children.
Emergency.offline: This page works even without internet after you open it once.

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.lead: Your privacy keeps you and your family safe. Here is what we collect and how long we keep it.
Privacy.collect1: One cookie that remembers your language. It does not track you.
Privacy.collect2: Basic visit counts without cookies, so we can see which pages help people. We do not use advertising trackers.
Privacy.collect3: If you fill out a form, only what you type in it. We never ask for your immigration status, Social Security number, or A-number on this website.
Privacy.keep1: Form requests that do not become a case: deleted after 90 days.
Privacy.keep2: Files sent by other lawyers through our referral page: deleted after 30 days.
Privacy.keep3: Appointment reminders: deleted 7 days after the appointment.
Privacy.share1: We do not sell your information.
Privacy.share2: If the government asks for information, the request goes to our managing attorney first, and we record every request.
Privacy.contactText: Call or write to our office with any privacy question.

Accessibility.title: Accessibility
Accessibility.lead: We want everyone to be able to use this website, including people who use screen readers, keyboards, or older phones.
Accessibility.goal: Our goal is to meet the WCAG 2.2 AA standard.
Accessibility.features: You can change the language at the top of every page, have the page read aloud, and open the emergency guide without internet after your first visit.
Accessibility.report: If something does not work for you, please call or email our office and tell us. We will fix it.
